protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 2 of 3; refute not confirm; verify ADV-D045-T1-01 landed
summary: ADV-D045-T1-01 landed but only for one of the two findings it applies to. Clause 1 now splits the three predecessor items into two named discharge methods -- execution for S31V3-01 and S31V3-02, byte comparison for S31V3-CX-A1 -- and the new classification is right for S31V3-CX-A1 and wrong for S31V3-02. I proved that empirically rather than arguing it: deleting the S31V3-02 disclosure from doesNotFailWhen, and then deleting the entire checker block, both leave the checker at PASS bound=1 unbound=7 exit 0. No execution can distinguish the repaired artifact from the unrepaired one for that finding, because the checker never reads doesNotFailWhen at all. Everything else is clean -- all eight digests match live bytes, clauses 2 through 4 are byte-identical at 093d5308 which I verified rather than accepted, the token-loss diff returns nothing, and every governed file is untouched. This is the finding I saw at turn 1 and declined on weak grounds; Codex graded the same class and the repair fixed its sibling instance, so I am recording it now rather than declining it twice.

objections.claim: The repair created a per-finding discharge-method taxonomy and then applied it inconsistently. S31V3-02 is still filed under 'discharged by execution', and no execution can produce evidence for it.
evidence: Clause 1 now reads: 'S31V3-01 and S31V3-02 are discharged by execution on these bytes. S31V3-CX-A1 is discharged by byte comparison with the pinned predecessor verdict tokens.'
S31V3-02 was my v3 finding that doesNotFailWhen omits the limit that produced the v2 blocker. Its v4 repair is a text entry, doesNotFailWhen[3]. Its presence is established by reading the JSON.

The checker never reads it. grep over check-section31-supplier-coverage-v4.py for doesNotFailWhen, failsWhen, and the checker block returns nothing. The only table fields the checker reads are counts, freezeSection31, and items -- with id, standing, textVerbatim, supplier, and within supplier path, selector and sha256.

Proved by mutation on a scratchpad copy: baseline PASS bound=1 unbound=7 exit 0; with doesNotFailWhen truncated to remove the S31V3-02 disclosure, PASS bound=1 unbound=7 exit 0; with the entire 'checker' block deleted from the table, still PASS bound=1 unbound=7 exit 0.

By contrast S31V3-01 belongs where it is: it is a code behaviour change, and I demonstrated it at the v4 review by running the identical mutation against both generations -- KeyError under checker v3, typed 'FAIL - S31-1: BOUND item has no supplier' under checker v4.
objections.whyItMatters: The discharge method is what a later auditor re-runs. For S31V3-CX-A1 the entry now names a method that produces the evidence -- compare the pinned verdict tokens byte for byte. For S31V3-02 it names a method that produces nothing: an auditor who executes the checker to confirm that discharge gets a PASS that would be identical if the disclosure had never been added, or if the whole checker block were deleted. That is precisely the defect ADV-D045-T1-01 identified for its sibling, and the entry has already conceded the principle by repairing that one.
objections.whyThisSeverity: The same severity Codex's finding carried, because it is the same defect in the same sentence. Grading it lower than the instance already repaired would be inconsistent, and the whole reason this turn exists is that this class of imprecision was judged worth a SHOULD-FIX. I note the repair is genuinely discharged -- v4 does carry doesNotFailWhen[3] and I confirmed at the v4 review that its claim about resolve() is true of the code -- so what is wrong is the stated method, not the fact of discharge.
objections.remedy: Move S31V3-02 to a method that produces its evidence. For example: 'S31V3-01 is discharged by execution on these bytes. S31V3-02 and S31V3-CX-A1 are discharged by byte comparison — the doesNotFailWhen disclosure and the pinned predecessor verdict tokens respectively.' If the intent is to credit that S31V3-02's claim about checker behaviour was confirmed against code, say that explicitly rather than folding it into execution.

reviewerSelfCorrection.what: At turn 1 I saw this exact issue and declined it. I wrote that clause 1 called all three 'discharged by execution' though S31V3-02 is a disclosure rather than a code path that can be run, and then declined on the grounds that the v4 dispatch framed all three that way, that my own v4 verdict used a section heading saying namedRepairsVerifiedByExecution, and that 'if that phrasing overstates, I overstated first'.
reviewerSelfCorrection.whyThatWasWrong: Two of my three reasons were about consistency with prior framing rather than about whether the statement is true. Having used a loose heading myself is not evidence that the heading was accurate, and declining to object because I would be objecting to my own earlier words puts my consistency ahead of the register's precision. Codex graded the class I had waved through, and the repair vindicates the principle.
reviewerSelfCorrection.correctionApplied: I tested the claim this turn instead of reasoning about who said it first, and the mutation result is unambiguous. Where I previously argued from provenance of a phrase, I now check whether the stated method produces the evidence. The remaining instance is recorded above at the severity its sibling received.

reviewerSelfCorrection.what: This is the second consecutive turn where a repair fixed one instance of a defect class rather than the class. Last turn I recorded that my own S31V3-01 was narrower than the class Codex generalized into S31V4-CX-A2; this turn the repair to ADV-D045-T1-01 corrects one of two mis-filed findings.
reviewerSelfCorrection.correctionApplied: When verifying a repair, enumerate every member of the class the finding names and check each, rather than checking that the flagged instance moved. That is how I found this one: I asked which of the three predecessor findings each named method actually fits, not whether the sentence had changed.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 4429bcdc956cb4b314370bfe5c0b1949633e3824944ed2831ee9b8dc1d750dce both times, matching the dispatch's expected digest. No drift.

ADV-D045-T1-01 partially landed, and the half that landed is correct. S31V3-CX-A1 was the uppercase-verdict-token repair -- a string value change whose evidence is a byte comparison, not a run -- and clause 1 now files it exactly that way. The disposition table's description of the repair matches what clause 1 actually says.

The attack 'still claims all three were discharged by execution' fails literally: the sentence no longer says all three. It fails in substance for one of the two remaining, S31V3-01, and does not fail for S31V3-02, which is the objection above.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all eight: instrument v4 97727684…, checker v4 a3092826…, Claude 2 v4 7bef5029…, Codex v4 1db18b81…, Claude 2 turn 1 efe58b52…, Codex turn 1 6e7f24eb…, COORD 3aec906f…, file 08 80fc55d1…. Each measured by me against live bytes.

My turn-1 verdict is characterized exactly: 'CONSENT, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX'. That is what I returned, including zero notes. The entry does not overstate my position or convert my declined observation into a finding I did not make.

I verified the prompt's byte-identity claim rather than accepting it. I extracted the clause 2 through clause 4 span from both drafts independently and hashed it: 093d53087e8d5a52a86ee4264d44c2da for both. A token-loss diff over the whole draft returns NOTHING lost, so this repair is purely additive and the silent-drop failure mode does not recur.

Because clauses 2 through 4 are byte-identical, my turn-1 verification of them carries: SATISFIED occurs once in the refusal 'It is not SATISFIED evidence'; Phase-1A occurs in 'It is not the Phase-1A packet' and the rejected alternative; clause 3 opens the unmet list with 'the seven UNBOUND items'; and clause 4 carries the full condition block, the MF-6 citation and D-038's forward-warning, which I established at turn 1 is byte-identical to D-043's adopted clause 4.

The attack 'treats S31V4-01 / S31V4-02 / S31V4-CX-A1 / S31V4-CX-A2 as discharged' fails. Clause 3 names all four and closes 'Those advisories remain owed on a successor.' Both of my ids are present and accurately described, including the D-044 causation for S31V4-02.

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED, Phase-1A insertion, or condition-1 discharge', 'treats bound=1 / unbound=7 as complete coverage', and 'file-08 edited without MF-6' all fail. Condition 1 is expressly denied discharge in clause 4, and git reports file 08, the freeze, the blueprint and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md all unmodified, so nothing has been pre-applied ahead of adoption.

The checker's actual read surface is narrower than the table it validates, which is the fact the objection rests on: it reads table['counts'], table['freezeSection31'] and table['items'], and within items only id, standing, textVerbatim and supplier, and within supplier only path, selector and sha256. The entire checker block of the JSON -- failsWhen, doesNotFailWhen, path -- is documentation that no code reads.

The merits of section31-supplier-coverage.v4 and checker v4 beyond my separate review at 7bef5029, whose stated limits I carry forward: resolve() untested on selector forms the single bound row does not exercise, and no corpus sweep for candidate suppliers for the seven UNBOUND items.

nonConsentNote: I do not CONSENT, on one SHOULD-FIX, and the position deserves stating plainly because I consented at turn 1. I saw this issue then, declined it partly because I had used the same loose phrasing in my own v4 verdict, and that was the wrong basis -- who first used a phrase has no bearing on whether it is accurate. Codex graded the class, the repair conceded the principle and split the three findings by discharge method, and one of the two remaining assignments does not survive testing: deleting the S31V3-02 disclosure, or the entire checker block, changes nothing about what the checker prints. The remedy is one clause, and the entry has already shown at S31V3-CX-A1 exactly how to write it.
